items.text: Greetings Agents!
We're excited to let you know that we have rolled out a MAJOR UPDATE. This update addresses several issues that have been brought to our attention by the helpful community!
These issues run the gamut from tweaks, to bug fixes and degrinding.

Have you ever wanted to hire an agent and you just thought that their rate was a bit too pricey? Fear no more! The Agency Union has been busted, and agent rates have been reduced by 25% across the board.

"Ugh, 327 more Security cases until I can unlock Agent Wheeler to level 10?!" shakes fist furiously at devs Well, that sentiment and those like it are a thing of the past. No more endless hours of grinding to level up your agents.
We've generously increased the payout of all contracts and tiers across the board, because...you're worth it.
We've decreased the case officer reputation required to level up all of the case officers. No more snide remarks from disappointed case officers who disappointedly shake their heads.
The cost of items has been reduced by 25%. If you've been eying the Tier 4 Thumper 187 Shotgun, with prices like these, why not pick up two?
Achievement icons updated
LQA fixes for achievements, puzzle data, tutorial hints, and general text.
Operation lead activation fixed

Do we REALLY need to write this? It took us a while to come around, but at the end of the day we want you, the players to HAVE FUN. It was a bit of a wake-up call when we realized that although a lot of players had sunk endless hours into the game, only a small percentage of players actually finished it. The grindy aspect seems to have prevented players from delving deeper into the story and experiencing the intricate plot twists we've lovingly created.
We hope that you enjoy this update!
We've had hundreds of streamers check out the game so far, check out some of the Youtube Shorts from their gamplay experiences on the official Rough Justice: '84 Youtube Channel.
Map Overview mode: Simply press "M" and get a complete overview of all of your agents and cases! (this pauses the game) Make sure your agents aren't just idling around- time is money!
Auto-Save/Quick-Save functionality: This is 1984- welcome to the future! Our retro circuits have been rerouted enabling auto save and quick saves!

So, it's been a few days since we released, and you guys have been amazing with pointing out the bugs you've found. For those of you that find any more bugs, feel free to hit us up on our discord and post them in the bug reports channel. Alternatively, you can use the in-game bug logging feature in the main menu.

We launched our Alpha Demo about two months ago as part of the Steam Next Fest, and we've been busy watching streamers and gathering feedback. We decided to leave the Alpha Demo up on Steam, for now, however, we will not be pushing updates to that particular build.

As a small indie dev team, we have to focus our attention on the further development of the game, and maintaining two parallel development branches would be very time-intensive. But don't fret, before we locked down the demo, we pushed a number of updates, so it's a fairly solid build.
We are planning on having a Beta Demo available in the Fall, so stay tuned! The Beta Demo will essentially be a vastly updated version with more bells and whistles than the Alpha.

PLEASE NOTE: The updates and bug fixes below are not reflected in the Alpha Demo, but rather in our experimental/nightly branch. If you would like access to our experimental build to test these changes, feel free to hop on our discord and ping us. We've already given a number of streamers access to this branch for further testing, and ofc so they can test their skills on the newly balanced puzzles, to compete for bragging rights ;)
Below we've listed, in no particular order some of the new features that are currently in the experimental build.

We've completely revamped the game settings! Now you can choose the exact resolution you'd like to play the game in, as well as whether you'd like to play in windowed mode, because...I guess that's a thing?

In the previous build, rolling double 1's would give you an automatic case fail, but we've taken it a step further ;) Now, not only do you lose, but you have to choose a negative card. Talk about adding insult to injury, amirite?

This is a feature that many players requested, and it gives you an increased chance of being able to hire the agent that you want. A good example of utilizing this feature to min/max, would be if you have an agent that you really like, but their shift ends, and they clock off; but you'd really like to hire them again. Without paying for a refresh, you may end up waiting for 3 hours only to find that they're STILL not available. Having the "pay to refresh" functionality isn't a sure-fire way of ensuring that the agent you want is going to become available, but the odds are dramatically increased.

As a small indie dev team, we have to focus our attention on the further development of the game, and maintaining two parallel development branches would be very time-intensive. But don't fret, before we locked down the demo, we pushed a number of updates, so it's a fairly solid build.

If you would like access to our experimental build to test these changes, feel free to hop on our discord and ping us. We've already given a number of streamers access to this branch for further testing, and ofc so they can test their skills on the newly balanced puzzles, to compete for bragging rights ;)
Below we've listed, in no particular order some of the new features that are currently in the experimental build.

Having this new feature implemented is going to be a huge game-changer- literally! This allows us to test mid to late-game balancing, as well as giving us a lot more freedom to jump right back into the fray.

After watching countless hours of streamers trying to send agents on cases and clicking on the wrong button, we knew something had to be done. The new "cocking" feature(?) required you to click on the agent and then they are prepared, and then you send them on their merry little way.
We've come to realize more and more how attached players get to their agents, so we decided to jazz things up a bit and have a bit of bling!
One of the other major frustrations for players was the use of gear during cases. Previously you had to find the little "gear" icon- and then choose it- now gear cards are shown by default.

items.text: We soft-launched our Alpha Demo about a week ago and we've had plenty of time to gather input.
The number one gripe that a lot of players had was the lack of proper onboarding, which we've now addressed.

After our initial hotfix to squash a number of nasty bugs we focused on dissecting the general feedback from players and streamers. Thanks to the good folks over at G.Round we've been making massive headway, and their input has been invaluable. So, a big shout out to all of the awesome folks over there!

This is a mechanic that we had been planning on implementing at a later date, but due to the feedback received, we prioritized it. Immersion is everything, and coming to grips with a brand new game with different mechanics can sometimes be a daunting experience.

Watching streamers become frustrated because they weren't sure about the correlation of certain mechanics was as equally as frustrating for us! We wanted to make the onboarding as enjoyable and straightforward as possible, and we hope we've achieved this.
Probably the second most requested feature was the ability to select different difficulty levels with the puzzles. As previously mentioned, there are 3 different Tiers of difficulty for cases:
Tier 1 = Easy
Tier 2 = Normal
Tier 3 = Hard

This is not only reflected in the number of successful rolls required during a case, but also in the puzzles. This change however only concerns the training center, If you'll remember, the purpose of the training center is to give players an opportunity to try out all of the puzzles and prepare themselves for their usage within cases. Having the ability to choose the difficulty level is essential in this process, as puzzles scale according to case tier difficulty!

Even with the initial addition of the 3 tiers of puzzle difficulty, we realized that it is a lost opportunity not to add a "Tier 0" and a "Tier 4". With these additions we are able to slowly introduce puzzles to new players [Tier 0] and of course challenge the most hardcore members of the community [Tier 4].
TUTORIAL ONBOARDING!
